# Bibliography and Index (File Pages 401–415)

**Nature of the section.** File pages 401 through 408 are the tail of the book's reference list, running alphabetically from Stenning and Oberlander (1995) through song and story permissions ("The Marvelous Toy," "Automation," "They're Made of Meat," "The Hunter," "This Land is Your Land," "Get Together," "Aquarius," "Imagine," "Evr'y Time We Say Goodbye") (file pages 401–408). File pages 409 through 415 open the Index, covering entries from Abbott through "Cognitive Psychology" (file pages 409–415). No prose argument by Steven Pinker appears here, so there are no source claims to summarize, no reasoning chains to reconstruct, and no explicit limits or disagreements to report. Printed page labels are visible as bracketed numbers in the running text — {622} on file page 402, {623} on 403, {624} on 404, {625} on 406, {629} on 408, {630} on 409, {631} on 411, {632} on 412, {633} on 414, {634} on 415 — but these are OCR artifacts of the printed pagination and should not be treated as file positions.

**What the index does reveal, as a map rather than as argument.** The index shows which topics the book treats and where, which is useful for locating the real chapters on representation, perception, learning, and reasoning. Entries relevant to a thinking machine include "Artificial intelligence" with sub-entries for emotions, goal-seeking, literature, reasoning, robotics, and vision (file page 411); "Artificial Life" (411); "Associationism" and "Auto-associators" (411); "Bayesian inference" split into perception and reasoning (412); "Belief-desire psychology" (412); "Case-based reasoning" (414); "Categorization" (414); "Cheater detectors" (414); "Chinese Room" (415); "Cognitive niche" (415); and "Cognitive Psychology" (415). Perception is indexed under "Auditory perception," "Attention, visual," "Agnosia," "Blindsight," "Ames," and "Bayesian inference … in perception" (file pages 410–413). Memory appears as "Bulletin board, mental" (414) and "Auto-associators" (411). Emotion appears under "Amygdala," "Anger," "Animal emotions," and "Artificial intelligence: Emotions" (410–411). Social cognition appears under "Belief-desire psychology," "Coalitional psychology," and "Cheater detectors" (412, 414). Creativity appears only as a citation to Weisberg (405) and under "Case-based reasoning" (414). Analogy, time, and causation are not visible in this slice.

**Engineering implications, clearly separated.** For our design work, this section is a finding aid, not evidence. It tells us that the book devotes substantial treatment to computational vision, Bayesian perception, categorization, goal-directed behavior, and belief-desire reasoning, and that these are the chapters to read for grounded mechanisms. It does not license any claim that a rule's permitted scope has been distinguished from memorization here, nor that innate capacities have been separated from acquired knowledge; those questions must be answered from the body chapters. Nothing in an index entry demonstrates a working mechanism, and no entry establishes that a non-neural inspectable machine is sufficient for human intelligence or consciousness.

**Uncertainty and garbling.** The OCR is visibly degraded: "graphical andlinguistic" (401), "Surpijo" for a coauthor name (401), "Biilthoff" and "Bulthoff" for Bülthoff (402, 414), "Ant6n" (401), "Cognitive Psychology, J2" for volume 12 (404), "Cognition, IS" for volume 15 (406), "EMIU" for EMI (408), and run-together words throughout. Index sub-entries use inconsistent indentation and spacing, so page ranges should be verified against a clean copy before being cited as authoritative. The boldface convention for section-dedicated page ranges is stated on file page 409 but cannot be reliably recovered from this text stream, since bold is not preserved.
